heading: Attribution graphs on a large model's own neurons explain behaviour without a stand-in model
definition: attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons explain its behaviour without a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
summary: Two independent groups find attribution graphs built from neurons in 2B–9B Gemma and Llama models faithful and competitive with stand-in graphs built on SAEs or transcoders, though some transcoders still score higher. The limits depend on task and model: Gemma-2-2B subject–verb agreement circuits need about 50,000 neurons to recover half the task performance, Llama-3.1 neuron circuits on ARC score close to random, and above 9B there are only the original's single-prompt demonstrations.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: none. <1B: mixed. In Pythia-70M, neuron circuits need about 1500 neurons for half of SVA performance (2403.19647, limits_scope). The authors judged essentially none of the Bias in Bios neurons interpretable (2403.19647; the checker relabels this verdict from challenges to limits_scope). The purpose-built 274.2M MoWE path supports only partly (2611.03655). 1-10B: R2 with task-dependent limits. Support comes from 2601.22594 (Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma-2-2B/9B) and 2610.24521 (Gemma 3 4B). After the checks, the only challenges verdict is 2504.13151 on Llama-3.1 ARC Easy/Challenge: NAP/NAP-IG CMD 0.67-0.69 vs random 0.74, and CPR 0.26 (at random). In the same study, Gemma-2 ARC Easy neuron circuits are well above random (CMD 0.28-0.33 vs 0.68; CPR 1.01-1.53). Limits come from 2403.19647 (Gemma-2-2B: about 50000 neurons for half of SVA performance; Bias in Bios neurons judged uninterpretable) and from 2504.13151 (IOI/arithmetic node circuits are above random but short of edge-level EAP-IG). 10-100B: R0 (original only: Qwen3-32B, two single-prompt ablations). >100B: R0 (original only: Kimi K3, one graph, no ablation).
suggested_status.reason: counts: V5.studies_tested = 6, with V5.tested_by_tranche T1 = 1 (the original) and T2 = 5. V5.verdicts: supports 4 studies, limits_scope 5, challenges 2. counts.json was built before the checks. V5.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. Two studies outside the original's author group find neuron-basis circuits or graphs faithful and competitive with SAE or transcoder ones at 2B-9B. 2601.22594: reviewed, code, Llama and Gemma. 2610.24521: workshop, Gemma 3 4B. Its Figure 15 legend summaries state no L0 range: Replacement Score 0.64 for neurons vs 0.55 for TopK, below 0.74 for Gemmascope L0-big. Its text says both Gemmascopes score higher than neurons around L0 10-100. V5.studies_by_size shows no study other than the original above 9B. The checks change the challenges side in two ways. (1) The checker relabels 2403.19647's Bias in Bios verdict as limits_scope: 70M/2B models, no BiB neuron circuit tested for faithfulness, and the evidence is a qualitative interpretability judgment plus an editing skyline. Its SVA verdict (about 50000 Gemma-2-2B neurons for half of SVA performance) was already limits_scope, so this study now gives no challenge. (2) 2504.13151's ARC challenge holds only for Llama-3.1 ARC Easy/Challenge (CMD 0.67-0.69 vs random 0.74; CPR 0.26). The checker reads Gemma-2 ARC Easy (CMD 0.28-0.33 vs random 0.68; CPR 1.01-1.53) as supports. The remaining challenge, Llama-3.1 ARC, is on a task and setup other than the original's and does not replicate the original's graphs. So C is not suggested here; Iris may weigh it differently.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent neuron-graph test on a 10B+ model would decide the level at 10-100B. For example: Qwen3-32B with the original's prompts, with a quantitative fidelity measure against transcoder graphs on the same prompts. Rerunning MIB's Llama-3.1 ARC task with RelP on MLP activations would show whether the only remaining challenge survives the basis and attribution that 2601.22594 reports as best. If it survives, C becomes a candidate at 1-10B. Note that MIB's 'neurons' are single dimensions of submodule outputs, not MLP hidden units (checker note on 2504.13151). 2403.19647's neurons are basis-aligned directions in the MLP, residual-stream and attention-out sublayers, attributed with attribution patching / integrated-gradient approximations, with SVA nodes counted per token position (checker correction on V5.conflicts[0]). Rerunning its Gemma-2-2B SVA circuit with RelP on MLP activations would show whether its circuit-size limit holds there. The pack does not show whether 2601.22594 and 2610.24521 share authors with each other.

original_result.setup: Attribution graphs were built directly from Qwen3-32B's MLP neurons and from Kimi K3's neurons, with no stand-in replacement model, and chosen Qwen3-32B neurons were switched off (ablated) on single prompts.
original_result.result: In Qwen3-32B, on a preeclampsia prompt, removing four neurons that act as hubs for the diagnosis changed the answer from 'visual disturbances' (0.90) to a question about itching. Removing eight neurons whose negative side encodes Santa cut the probability of a near-certain 'Santa' answer to 6%, versus 76% after removing twenty Christmas or Santa neurons; a neuron-only Kimi K3 graph for a found-wallet prompt was easy to read but was not tested by removing neurons.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Neuron circuits for multiple-choice QA in Qwen-2.5, Gemma-2 and Llama-3.1 beat random, rivaling edge-based circuits.
About 200 Llama 3.1 8B neurons matched SAE circuits, with no error nodes.
Gemma 3 4B neuron graphs matched TopK-transcoder graphs on replacement score without training a transcoder.
In a custom MoWE model, zeroing each unit of a traced four-unit path beat 95th-percentile alternatives.
Neuron circuits became faithful only at large sizes, needing far more nodes than features.
Neuron circuits for indirect-object identification (IOI) and arithmetic beat random but trailed edge-based EAP-IG circuits.
Neuron circuits matched SAE-circuit sparsity only with RelP attribution; comprehensive ones were too big to interpret.
Gemma 3 4B neuron graphs trailed Gemmascope transcoders and needed a trained linear correction.
Ablating a custom MoWE model's traced path cut the answer's logit but barely moved its probability.
Almost no flagged Bias in Bios classifier neurons were interpretable, so neuron-based SHIFT debiasing was abandoned.
Llama-3.1 neuron-level circuits for ARC Easy and Challenge performed no better than random.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: No independent quantitative test of neuron graphs above 9B. Outside the original, the largest model with a faithfulness or ablation test is Gemma-2-9B (2601.22594). 2610.24521 compares Replacement Score only on Gemma 3 4B (Fig 15). The same study also builds neuron RelP attribution graphs on Gemma 3 27B-it (a distress/apology circuit, features filtered by Claude Haiku; Fig 16, App L-M) and Gemma 4 26B-A4B (23 prompts, expert-influence Gini only; App N). Neither has a Replacement Score or an ablation (checker, text; no row). At 10-100B and at unstated (multi-trillion) size, all ablation evidence comes from the original: Qwen3-32B, two single prompts with ablation (R18, R19), and Kimi K3, one graph without ablation (R20). Another group's graphs at 26-27B add qualitative evidence of the same kind as the original's Kimi K3 graph. They add no fidelity measure.

untested.what: Explaining a model's behaviour beyond narrow tasks is untested. The tested tasks are SVA, Bias in Bios, IOI, MCQA, arithmetic, ARC, state capitals, small case studies, one MoWE prompt and 30 random prompts. No independent study measures how much of a model's general behaviour neuron graphs explain.

wording_issues.issue: Independent quantitative tests stay at or below 9B. MIB runs neuron node circuits on GPT-2 Small (117M), Qwen-2.5 0.5B, Gemma-2 2B and Llama-3.1 8B, a range of 117M–8B. 2601.22594 uses Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B (R7). 2610.24521 compares Replacement Scores on Gemma 3 4B only (R31). It also draws neuron RelP graphs on Gemma 3 27B-it and Gemma 4 26B-A4B, but reports no Replacement Score or ablation for them. One supporting study uses MoWE, a purpose-built 274.2M routed architecture with 'native coordinates', not a standard model's neurons (r11). Only the original reports Qwen3-32B and Kimi K3.

Which neuron basis is used matters, and the studies mean different things by 'neurons'. In 2601.22594, MLP-activation circuits are about 100x sparser than MLP-output circuits: R1 (Llama 3.1 8B, IG) and R5 (Gemma-2-2B). 2403.19647 defines a neuron as a basis-aligned direction, not necessarily after a nonlinearity (fn. 1). It takes neurons in MLPs, the layer-end residual stream and the attention out-projection (App. D.2), and on SVA it counts nodes per token position (App. A.2). Its neuron circuits needed about 1500 (Pythia-70M) and about 50000 (Gemma-2-2B) to explain half of SVA performance. In MIB, 'neurons' are single dimensions of submodule outputs (size d_model), not MLP hidden units.

Explanation is partial and depends on the task and the model. Edge-level neuron graphs (RelP with stop-grads) reach just over 80% faithfulness with about 10^5 edges (2601.22594 §5.4, Figure 5; text). On Gemma 3 4B, the Figure 15 legend summaries give neurons (RelP, k=128) a Replacement Score of 0.64 and Gemmascope L0-big 0.74. The legend states no L0 range, and the text says both Gemmascopes score higher than neurons around L0 10–100 (2610.24521). MoWE joint path ablation moves degrees probability only from 0.715 to 0.670. In MIB, neuron node circuits on ARC Easy and Challenge score at random only on Llama-3.1 (NAP and NAP-IG CPR 0.26). On Gemma-2 ARC Easy they are well above random (NAP CPR 1.01, NAP-IG CPR 1.53).

wording_issues.phrase: without a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error
wording_issues.issue: In 2610.24521 on Gemma 3 4B, replacement models built from top-k pruned neurons without correction have high KL and FVU above 1. A trained linear map on the pruned MLP output brings KL below the transcoders' (Section 2.2, Fig 3a; text). App A.1 says the FVU above 1 is specific to Gemma 3 4B, likely because of its post-feedforward LayerNorm. It also says the transcoders have higher KL than the neuron variants across models. These results concern replacement models built from neurons, not the study's RelP neuron graphs. 2601.22594 reports neuron circuits that avoid SAE error nodes (R2, R3).

Much of the independent evidence is node circuits evaluated by faithfulness or completeness, not graphs with neuron-to-neuron edges. MIB's NAP and NAP-IG circuits are node-level, and its untested line says it has no neuron-to-neuron edges. MoWE builds no attribution graph. On one prompt, it zeroes each of 722 active coordinates and records a 722 x 722 influence matrix over later coordinates. It reports one selected four-coordinate path, with coordinate-to-coordinate drops of 0.90, 0.84 and 1.42 and a coordinate-to-logit drop of 0.74 (r11). No full graph is reported or scored for faithfulness. The edge-level graphs come from 2601.22594 §5.4 and 2610.24521.

If 'explain' means human-readable: in the Bias in Bios classifier circuits (Pythia-70M, Gemma-2-2B), the authors abandoned SHIFT with neurons because essentially none of the implicated neurons were interpretable (2403.19647 §4; App. D.2, Figs 21–22). This is the authors' qualitative judgment, and no Bias in Bios neuron circuit is tested for faithfulness. Crowdworkers gave the top-30 Pythia-70M Bias in Bios neurons a mean rating of 36.0/100 (Table 7; text, no V5 row). 2601.22594 says a reasonably comprehensive circuit has too many neurons for a human 'to easily interpret' (Limitations). Its interpretable state-capitals circuit needed manual selection of 23 of 257 traced neurons (§6.1).

method_sensitivity.factor: Neuron representation (MLP activations vs MLP outputs)
method_sensitivity.what: MLP-activation neuron circuits are about 100x sparser than MLP-output circuits at comparable faithfulness. This holds in Llama 3.1 8B under IG (R1) and in Gemma-2-2B (R5); in Gemma-2-9B, MLP activations give substantially sparser circuits (R7). SVA, paired data.

In Llama 3.1 8B base on paired SVA, RelP gives about 200-neuron circuits with near-perfect faithfulness and completeness, at parity with SAE circuits (R2, R3). With IG, neuron circuits stay somewhat less sparse than SAE circuits (R1). The not-in-rows line says RelP still beats IG with unpaired data and zero ablation (Appendix D, Figure 8).

method_sensitivity.factor: Task and metric (MIB), with a model difference on ARC
method_sensitivity.what: MIB, neuron-level node circuits (NAP, NAP-IG); from the text (Tables 2, 14), no rows. MCQA, CPR (higher is better): NAP 0.38 (Qwen-2.5), 1.47 (Gemma-2), 1.69 (Llama-3.1); NAP-IG 0.77, 1.71, 1.87; random about 0.26–0.32; edge-level EAP-IG-inputs 1.16, 1.64, 1.05. MCQA, CMD (lower is better): NAP 0.30–0.35, NAP-IG 0.18–0.33; random 0.68–0.74; EAP-IG 0.05–0.14. IOI and arithmetic, CMD: NAP/NAP-IG 0.18–0.38; random 0.69–0.75; EAP-IG 0.00–0.04. ARC Easy/Challenge on Llama-3.1: CMD 0.67–0.69 vs random 0.74; CPR 0.26, at random. ARC Easy on Gemma-2: CMD 0.28–0.33 vs random 0.68; CPR 1.01 (NAP) and 1.53 (NAP-IG). Neuron circuits are at random only on Llama-3.1 ARC.

method_sensitivity.factor: Which trained transcoder is the comparator, and L0
method_sensitivity.what: Gemma 3 4B, 30 prompts, Replacement Score (RS). The Figure 15 legend gives per-method summaries with no L0 range stated: neuron graphs (RelP, k=128) 0.64, TopK transcoder (k=64) 0.55, Gemmascope L0-small 0.56, Gemmascope L0-big 0.74 (R31–R34; the reader had recorded 'figure only'). Section 2.4: around L0 10–100, both Gemmascope transcoders, but not TopK, have higher RS than the sparsified MLPs. Figure caption: L0-big dominates at high L0, and L0-big and L0-small are best at low L0. Whether neurons look sufficient depends on which transcoder is the comparator and on the L0 range.

method_sensitivity.factor: Trained linear correction on pruned neurons
method_sensitivity.what: Gemma 3 4B: replacement models from top-k pruned neurons without correction give high KL and FVU above 1. With a trained linear map on the neuron outputs, KL falls below the transcoders' (Section 2.2, Figure 3a, Appendix A.1; text, no row).

On the same SVA neuron-circuit evaluation, about 1500 neurons explain half the performance in Pythia-70M (r1) against about 50000 in Gemma-2-2B (r2). Hundreds of neurons must be ablated to remove performance in Pythia-70M (r3), against thousands in Gemma-2-2B (r4). The study's method-sensitivity line says the circuit-size comparisons differ between the two models.
